tier_reason: First-party docs page compares AMGCL with PETSc and Trilinos ML on a 3D Poisson problem (3,375,000 unknowns) on dual Xeon E5-2640 v3 and states the 20-100% / 4-7x setup claims verbatim; compiler and flags are not given, so not A, and it is not peer-reviewed or independent.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Shared-memory 3D Poisson (3,375,000 unknowns): AMGCL setup about 20-100% faster than Trilinos ML and 4-7 times faster than PETSc; overall CPU performance on par with Trilinos. With the CUDA backend the solve phase (without setup) is 3-4x faster than the CPU versions, but total time is only about 30% better than AMGCL/OpenMP or Trilinos ML.
corrections.caveats: First-party docs page; compiler flags not stated; hardware is old (Xeon E5-2640 v3, Tesla K80). The win is mainly in setup time; overall CPU performance is on par with Trilinos, and PETSc scales better. Smoothers differ between libraries (AMGCL SPAI0; Trilinos symmetric Gauss-Seidel; PETSc damped Jacobi, both on defaults). Distributed-memory runs on the same page show AMGCL about 3x worse than Trilinos AMG in one weak-scaling test and 2.5x slower at 384 cores in another. GPU speedup is over CPU AMGCL, not over a baseline library.

notes: Numbers verified on the page (docs/benchmarks.rst). The record's metric 'build-time' really means AMG solver setup time; the orchestrator may want to relabel it (metric is not a correctable field). The arXiv paper 1811.05704 only says performance is 'on par with alternative implementations', so no B upgrade.

tier_reason: First-party benchmarks/README.md table compares against cuSPARSE ALG2 and cuSPARSE SpMVOp ALG1/ALG2 on H100 PCIe with CUDA/cuSPARSE versions and protocol; the benchmark client is public but the core is a closed binary and no host compiler, flags or CPU are stated, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Geometric-mean execution-time speedup over cuSPARSE ALG2 (cusparseSpMV), preprocessing excluded, fp64, H100 PCIe: SpMV(1,0) 2.17x Mittelmann (20.25 vs 43.85 us), 1.64x MIPLIB nnz>10M (141.54 vs 232.66 us), 1.31x SuiteSparse nnz>10M (211.03 vs 275.97 us); SpMV(alpha,beta) 2.22x / 1.60x / 1.30x. Over cuSPARSE SpMVOp ALG1/ALG2: 1.38-1.69x.
corrections.caveats: Core is a closed binary under the ISpMV Binary License (source private); only interfaces, examples and the benchmark client are MIT. Speedups exclude ISpMV preprocessing, which costs 37-110 ms per direction (geometric mean), so it pays off only for repeated SpMV with a fixed matrix. Host compiler, flags and CPU not stated. Results include directions that failed the numerical criterion (README says the same failures occur for the baselines). Brand-new repo (single commit, v0.1.0 on 2026-09-30). Baseline cuSPARSE is not on the list.

notes: Re-opened the benchmark page and checked the speedups row by row: the search agent's 2.17x / 1.64x / 1.31x figures match the cuSPARSE ALG2 column for SpMV(1,0). usability 'reference' kept (the core is not copyable).
